name: canso
description: Spaceport Nova Scotia (Canso), Nova Scotia, Canada. Every value here is configuration; none is repeated in Python source.
vehicle_profile_source: The vehicle the site is configured for: the Cyclone-4M of the Abbreviated User's Guide, whose section 2.2 gives the pad coordinates above. backend.engine.ephemeris draws the ascent of this profile when a caller names no vehicle.
coordinate_source: Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide section 2.2, pad 45.3 N 61.0 W. Spec II.1 records this as VERIFIED (SCIENCE Sec F.2).

coordinate_variants.source: alternate published coordinates recorded in spec II.1, SCIENCE Sec G.3
alternate published coordinates recorded in spec II.1, SCIENCE Sec G.3

direction_policy.statement: all launches are conducted to the south over the Atlantic Ocean
direction_policy.source: Canso Spaceport Facility Environmental Assessment Registration Document, Strum Consulting for MLS, June 2018, Project 16-5903, sections 2.2.5 and 2.2.5.4
direction_policy.applies_to: this site only. The hazard screen reads the admissible direction from the site file; a site whose file states no policy is judged by its corridor bounds alone.

corridor.source: DERIVED, backend/engine/data/derive_canso_corridor.py. Nominal flown azimuths from spec (II.2) at the Reg Doc pad latitude 45.3104 N: 51.6 deg -> 117.98, 87.9 deg -> 177.01, 98.1 deg -> 191.56 (AUG 2.4.1/2.5.1, VERIFIED inputs); minus/plus a 3.0 deg dispersion half-width covering ~6x the demonstrated 0.52 deg lofted offset (AUG 118.5 vs 117.98); rounded to 1 deg resolution. Great-circle geography checks recorded in the derivation script: east ray over open Atlantic, Little Dover bypass consistent with the AUG T+75 s manoeuvre, Newfoundland clears by >150 km, 2000 km endpoints in open Atlantic. The EA publishes no numeric corridor (Reg Doc Figure 2.9 is a two-panel illustration with no degree axis); these bounds are DERIVED, not VERIFIED.
corridor.derivation: backend/engine/data/derive_canso_corridor.py:derive_corridor_bounds(); test_range_closeout_derivation.py asserts the committed bounds reproduce it
assumptions: The 3.0 deg dispersion half-width is a judgement covering ~6x the demonstrated 0.52 deg lofted-trajectory offset; it is not a published 3-sigma figure.

The single interval [115, 195] is the envelope over the three occupied flown bands ([115,121], [174,180], [188.6,194.6]); mid-fan azimuths such as 150 deg (i=69.4) are geometrically admitted but correspond to no advertised mission, so the envelope is conservative.

A_min = 115 rests on 51.6 deg being the lowest advertised inclination with a published azimuth (AUG 2.4.1); due-east 90 deg tracks over open ocean but no advertised mission flies it and the EA direction statement is southbound.
corridor.pending_verification: Environmental assessment Figure 2.9 three-sigma corridor check (SCIENCE Sec G.2); a published numeric corridor would supersede these DERIVED bounds

car_source: Canadian Aviation Regulations 602.43 and 602.44, the launch authorization path recorded in spec II.8 and II.10. Referenced as static regulatory provenance; not parsed by the engine.

operating_hours.restriction: none published; engine treats all hours admissible
assumptions: No published operating-hours RESTRICTION for Canso was located, so the engine treats all hours as admissible and operating hours never silently removes a window from a search. This is a NARROW explicit statement, not a claim about nominal practice: the Registration Document sections 2.2.5 and 2.2.5.4 state the NOMINAL expectation that 'the majority of launches will be conducted between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 12:00 p.m.' (local), coordinated with Transport Canada and Nav Canada, which is a majority-practice note rather than a range restriction.
documents_checked: Canso Spaceport Facility Environmental Assessment Registration Document, Strum Consulting for MLS, June 2018, Project 16-5903, sections 2.2.5 and 2.2.5.4 (nominal 7:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. note; all launches south over the Atlantic; no time-of-day restriction; no approval-condition time window in the federal/provincial approvals tables 1.3/1.4)
Canso Spaceport Facility Focus Report, March 2019 (no operating-hours restriction located)
EA review comments file Comments.txt, 5027 lines incl. reviewer terms-and-conditions discussion (no time-of-day launch condition located)
Cyclone-4M Abbreviated User's Guide Version 2, 2019-05-15, via web.archive.org (no operating-hours restriction located)

conjunction.source: Spec II.8 names config key conjunction.miss_threshold_km and states the default is an ASSUMPTION value pending range feedback. 50 km is the engine default; no published Canso range feedback exists.

CUSTOM.source: Spec IV.1 type mapping: CUSTOM takes explicit h_t_km and i_t_deg from the request, so it carries no default inclination or altitude.

LEO.source: 45.1 deg is the advertised LEO class inclination from the project public material (spec II.10, SCIENCE Sec F.1, VERIFIED).
assumptions: h_t_km = 400 for the class default. The advertised inclination is published but the class altitude is not. 400 km is chosen because it is the altitude at which the spec's own plane-change penalty of 26.8 m/s (spec II.5, v_c = 7.67 km/s) reproduces; at 600 km the same formula gives 25.15 m/s. Nodal drift is always computed at whatever altitude the request carries, so this default affects only the penalty of an unreachable target.

POLAR.source: OneWeb-class polar inclination 87.9 deg from the project public material (spec II.10, SCIENCE Sec F.1, VERIFIED).

SSO.source: 98.1 deg is the SSO inclination at roughly 650 to 700 km (spec II.6); 674 km is the altitude the spec pairs with it in the drift table.
